title: JSON Form Structure Validation
description: Validates JSON files against Minecraft documentation-derived form schemas. These schemas define the expected structure, types, and constraints for Minecraft content files like entity definitions, block definitions, spawn rules, etc. The validator checks type compatibility, value ranges, string lengths, required fields, enum values, and more based on metadata in form.json files.

101.title: Unexpected String Where Object Expected
101.description: A string value was found where an object was expected. The form schema expects this field to be an object with properties, not a scalar string.

102.title: Unexpected Boolean Where Object Expected
102.description: A boolean value was found where an object was expected. The form schema expects this field to be an object with properties, not a true/false value.

103.title: Unexpected Number Where Object Expected
103.description: A number value was found where an object was expected. The form schema expects this field to be an object with properties, not a numeric value.

110.title: Data Type Mismatch
110.description: The data type of a field does not match what the schema expects. For example, a string was provided where a number was expected, or an array was provided where an object was expected.
110.x-runtime-constraint-description: This is triggered when DataFormValidator.getDataMismatchError() finds the JavaScript typeof the data doesn't match any of the expected FieldDataType values for the field or its alternates.

111.title: Value Below Minimum
111.description: A numeric value is below the minimum allowed value defined in the schema. The field has a minValue constraint that this value violates.
111.x-runtime-constraint-description: Triggered when field.minValue is defined and the data value is less than minValue.

112.title: Value Above Maximum
112.description: A numeric value exceeds the maximum allowed value defined in the schema. The field has a maxValue constraint that this value violates.
112.x-runtime-constraint-description: Triggered when field.maxValue is defined and the data value is greater than maxValue.

113.title: String Too Short
113.description: A string value is shorter than the minimum length required by the schema. The field has a minLength constraint that this value violates.
113.x-runtime-constraint-description: Triggered when field.minLength is defined and data.length is less than minLength.

114.title: String Too Long
114.description: A string value exceeds the maximum length allowed by the schema. The field has a maxLength constraint that this value violates.
114.x-runtime-constraint-description: Triggered when field.maxLength is defined and data.length is greater than maxLength.

115.title: Value Not in Choices
115.description: The value is not one of the allowed choices defined in the schema. The field has a fixed set of valid values and the provided value is not among them.
115.x-runtime-constraint-description: Triggered when field.choices is defined, field.mustMatchChoices is not false, and the value is not found in the choices array.

116.title: Pattern Mismatch
116.description: A string value does not match the required pattern defined in the schema. The field has a validity condition with a regex pattern that the value must match.
116.x-runtime-constraint-description: Triggered when field.validity contains a condition with comparison=ComparisonType.matchesPattern and the regex test fails.

117.title: Array Length Mismatch
117.description: An array has a different number of elements than required by the schema. The field has a fixedLength constraint specifying exactly how many elements are expected.
117.x-runtime-constraint-description: Triggered when field.fixedLength is defined and the array length doesn't match.

118.title: Point/Range Size Mismatch
118.description: A point or range array has the wrong number of elements. Point2 requires exactly 2 elements [x, y], Point3 requires exactly 3 elements [x, y, z], and ranges require exactly 2 elements [min, max].
118.x-runtime-constraint-description: Triggered when the field dataType is point2 (expects 2), point3 (expects 3), floatRange (expects 2), or intRange (expects 2) and the array length doesn't match.

119.title: Key Not Allowed
119.description: A key in a keyed collection is not in the allowed keys list. The schema defines a specific set of valid keys for this collection.
119.x-runtime-constraint-description: Triggered when field.allowedKeys is defined for a keyed collection (keyedObjectCollection, keyedStringCollection, etc.) and a key in the data is not in the allowedKeys array.

120.title: Unexpected Property
120.description: An object contains a property that is not defined in the schema. This may indicate a typo, deprecated property, or use of an undocumented feature.
120.x-runtime-constraint-description: Triggered when form.strictAdditionalProperties is true and the data object contains a key not defined in form.fields. By default, this check is disabled for Minecraft content since many formats allow additional properties.

121.title: Missing Required Field
121.description: A required field is missing from the object. The schema indicates this field must be present for the content to work correctly.
121.x-runtime-constraint-description: Triggered when field.isRequired is true and the data for this field is undefined or null.

401.title: JSON Parse Error
401.description: Error when a JSON file could not be parsed for form validation. The file may have syntax errors such as missing commas, unquoted keys, trailing commas, or invalid escape sequences.
401.x-runtime-constraint-description: Triggered when StorageUtilities.getJsonObject() returns null due to a JSON.parse() failure.

402.title: Form Not Found
402.description: No documentation form schema was found for this JSON file type. The file format may not yet be documented in form.json files, or this project item type may not have a form path mapping.
402.x-runtime-constraint-description: Triggered when Database.ensureFormLoadedByPath() returns undefined for the form path returned by ProjectItemUtilities.getFormPathForType().
